verdict_reason: Two independently validated P1 false-success paths require correction before the reviewed source checkpoint can be relied upon. This source-only verdict does not authorize production launch or a benchmark.
intent: A Linux-only completion witness preserves protected owner context through actual HTTP hooks, waits for producer and trace completion, and fails closed on owner cancellation or hook failure. This is source-only and adds no listener, spending authority, or production admission.

evidence: engine/transport/patch_factory_gateway_completion.py:123 --             if gatewayCompletion != nil { _ = gatewayCompletion.HooksFinished(err) }

The actual patched handler at /home/bo/sfactory-witness-integration-mzybdfbh/green/source/transports/bifrost-http/handlers/inference.go:2211-2237 logs and continues when InterceptChunk returns a non-nil chunk with an error; no witness method receives this error.

The actual plugin interceptor at /home/bo/sfactory-witness-integration-mzybdfbh/green/source/transports/bifrost-http/lib/config.go:5965-5977 returns immediately on the first hook error, skipping any remaining chunk hooks.
engine/transport/factory_gateway_completion.go:153 -- 	if ctx.Err() != nil || w.ownerCtx.Err() != nil || w.failed || !w.hooksFinished || !w.producerFinished {

Retained patched handlers/inference.go:2129-2130 calls postHookCompleter() and passes only its error into HooksFinished; handlers/inference.go:2207-2234 calls interceptor.InterceptChunk and handles its error by sending an error, canceling the stream child, draining, and returning without recording failure.

Retained patched handlers/inference.go:2168 invokes runCompleter(false) on early return, then :2179 calls ProducerFinished after trace completion. With successful post hooks, the resulting HooksFinished(nil) and ProducerFinished allow Wait(owner) to succeed.

engine/transport/factory_gateway_completion_test.go:119-136 explicitly permits successful completion after cancellation of the stream child, so child cancel() does not compensate for the missing chunk-error latch.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sticky failure method to the witness, invoke it when the protected stream chunk interceptor returns any error, and stop sending the protected chunk; add real-handler regressions for both nil and non-nil error results and a later skipped hook.
findings.title: Fail the witness on stream chunk hook errors
findings.why_it_matters: A stream hook can return a non-nil chunk and an error. Bifrost stops executing the remaining chunk hooks but logs the error and continues sending that chunk; the witness later records successful post-hooks and producer completion, so its Wait can succeed despite the failed and skipped stream hooks. A downstream user of this witness could incorrectly accept an incomplete policy or transformation pipeline. Signal a sticky witness failure on every chunk interceptor error and abort protected stream output so failed hooks cannot be reported as complete.

evidence: engine/transport/patch_factory_gateway_completion.py:130 --             if gatewayCompletion != nil { _ = gatewayCompletion.ProducerFinished() }
Composed handlers/inference.go:2246-2250 calls sonic.Marshal(chunk), logs a non-nil error, and continues without signaling the witness.
Composed handlers/inference.go:2291-2300 runs the post-hook completer and sends [DONE] when no error chunk was transmitted; an omitted unserializable chunk sets no error marker.
Composed core/schemas/bifrost.go:1827 exposes RawResponse as interface{}, and the chat chunk MarshalJSON delegates to MarshalSorted for the chat response at lines 1961-1962.
findings.suggested_fix: Instrument the protected streaming handler's chunk serialization error branch to latch a sanitized completion failure and stop or drain the protected stream; add a real-handler regression whose chunk contains a non-serializable value and verify that neither a normal terminal result nor successful witness is possible.
findings.title: Dropped malformed stream chunk still earns completion
findings.why_it_matters: A protected stream can lose a response chunk while its client receives the normal terminal marker and the completion witness reports success. The inherited handler logs and skips a chunk that cannot be marshaled, then completes the post-hook and signals producer completion without reporting that loss. For example, a transport plugin can return a chat chunk whose RawResponse contains a non-JSON value without returning a hook error; the marker and witness cannot distinguish the resulting partial output. Latch serialization errors into the witness and fail the protected stream so incomplete output cannot be accepted as complete.

residual_risks: The test root is deliberately synthetic; this review does not establish peer authentication, production owner acquisition, or physical-call capture closure.
Static review only: this reviewer did not execute the Linux-only copied-package transport tests or mutate an isolated source stage.
testing_gaps: The actual-handler tests cancel owners only before middleware entry; the witness unit cancellation test cancels before acknowledgments. Add a channel-coordinated real-handler case that cancels the original owner while a post-hook or trace callback is blocked, then releases it and asserts Wait cannot succeed. This covers cancellation after successful admission, which the stated owner-lifetime contract also requires.
